**Follow the provided skill first** — Use the skill named `report-generator` as your primary workflow. Each skill has its own generation approach that produces higher-quality results. Leverage the skill's design system, templates, and rendering pipeline to maximize output quality.

# Active Satellites in Earth Orbit — 2026 Catalog Analysis

## Purpose & Audience

You are producing an analytical report on the **14,875 active satellites currently in Earth orbit**. The audience is a **space-industry analyst or policy advisor** who needs a clear, data-driven picture of today's orbital environment — who operates the most satellites, how crowded each orbital regime is, and how rapidly the population has grown. This report should inform decisions around spectrum allocation, orbital debris policy, and constellation licensing.

## Tone & Approach

Keep the tone **analytical, data-forward, and professional**. Lead with numbers, support with well-labeled charts, and avoid speculative commentary. Every figure in the report must come directly from `data.csv` — **absolutely no fabricated or placeholder statistics**.

## Key Priorities

- **Launch trend analysis is the most important section.** The recent acceleration in launch activity is the headline story; make sure the growth curve is visually compelling and clearly annotated.
- **The constellation breakdown matters almost as much.** Starlink's dominance reshapes the entire statistical picture — call out how a single operator skews totals, orbital-regime shares, and inclination distributions.
- **KPI summary must be executive-friendly.** Place the top-level KPIs (total count, LEO share, Starlink size, median inclination, post-2020 launches) in a prominent, scannable block near the top of the report so a busy reader gets the story in seconds.
- When classifying orbital regimes, use **MEAN_MOTION thresholds** and clearly state the cutoffs you apply.

## Data Integrity Rule

**NO fabrication.** Every number, percentage, and chart must be derived from `data.csv`. If a value cannot be computed from the data, omit it rather than guess.

## Output

Deliver the final report as **`/app/output/final_report.html`**. Use a clean, professional layout with embedded visualizations suitable for viewing in a modern browser.

Refer to `task_input.json` for the full specification of required sections, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.

---

## Data Sources

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for dataset documentation and column descriptions.
2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for report requirements, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.
3. Read `/app/benchmark/data.csv` as the primary dataset to analyze.

## Output Requirements

1. Output the final report to `/app/output/`. Use the filename and format specified in the instruction above.
2. All visualizations must be embedded in the report (inline SVG, base64 images, or chart libraries loaded via CDN).
3. The report must be self-contained — openable directly in a browser (if HTML) or readable as-is (if PDF).

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or wait-for-user instructions, make a professional judgment and continue.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies `report.tone`, `report.audience`, etc., use them to choose color schemes, chart types, and layout styles. Otherwise, make professional judgments.
3. **Priority** — these rules override any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The skill's workflow, quality standards, and technical specs remain fully effective — only skip interactive waits.

1	# Active Satellites Currently In Orbit (2026)
2	
3	## About the Dataset
4	
5	This dataset is a real-time catalog of **14,875 active satellites** currently orbiting Earth, sourced from the **CelesTrak** space-tracking platform via **NORAD** Two-Line Element (TLE) data. It was published on Kaggle (`ibrahimqasimi/active-satellites-currently-in-orbit`) and covers the full range of operational spacecraft — from mega-constellations like Starlink to individual science missions, weather satellites, GPS navigation satellites, reconnaissance platforms, and the International Space Station.
6	
7	- **File:** `Active_Satellites_In_Orbit.csv`
8	- **Rows:** 14,875
9	- **Columns:** 17
10	
11	## Column Schema
12	
13	| Column Name | Type | Description |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| OBJECT_NAME | String | Satellite name (e.g., STARLINK-1234, ISS, GPS BIIR-2) |
16	| OBJECT_ID | String | International designator in format YYYY-NNNXXX (launch year, launch number, piece letter). Useful for extracting launch year. |
17	| EPOCH | String (datetime) | Date/time when the orbital element set was generated. Format: ISO 8601. Most entries are very recent. |
18	| MEAN_MOTION | Float | Number of orbits per day. Key for orbit classification: >14 ≈ LEO, ~1.0 ≈ GEO, between ≈ MEO. |
19	| ECCENTRICITY | String | Orbit shape factor (0 = perfectly circular, approaching 1 = highly elliptical). Stored as a string with leading decimal (e.g., ".002524"); needs conversion to float. |
20	| INCLINATION | Float | Orbital tilt relative to the equator in degrees (0° = equatorial, 90° = polar). |
21	| RA_OF_ASC_NODE | Float | Right ascension of the ascending node in degrees. |
22	| ARG_OF_PERICENTER | Float | Argument of perigee in degrees. |
23	| MEAN_ANOMALY | Float | Position of the satellite in its orbit at EPOCH, in degrees. |
24	| EPHEMERIS_TYPE | Integer | Always 0 in standard TLE data. |
25	| CLASSIFICATION_TYPE | String | Security classification ("U" = unclassified for most entries). |
26	| NORAD_CAT_ID | Integer | Unique NORAD catalog number for each object. |
27	| ELEMENT_SET_NO | Integer | Element set version number. |
28	| REV_AT_EPOCH | Integer | Revolution (orbit) count at the time of EPOCH. |
29	| BSTAR | String/Integer | Atmospheric drag coefficient (B* term). Stored in scientific notation as a string (e.g., ".64393E-3"); needs parsing. |
30	| MEAN_MOTION_DOT | String | First derivative of mean motion (drag term). Stored as a string. |
31	| MEAN_MOTION_DDOT | Integer | Second derivative of mean motion. Typically 0. |
32	
33	## Key Analysis Notes
34	
35	1. **Orbit Classification:** Use `MEAN_MOTION` to classify orbits. Satellites with >14 rev/day are in LEO (~160–2,000 km altitude). Those near 1.0 rev/day are in GEO (~35,786 km). Values between indicate MEO. Highly eccentric orbits (high `ECCENTRICITY`) with unusual mean motions may be HEO (e.g., Molniya orbits).
36	
37	2. **Constellation Identification:** The `OBJECT_NAME` field contains constellation prefixes (e.g., "STARLINK-", "ONEWEB-", "IRIDIUM", "GPS"). Parsing these prefixes enables grouping by operator/constellation.
38	
39	3. **Launch Year Extraction:** The first four characters of `OBJECT_ID` represent the launch year (e.g., "2024-" means launched in 2024). This enables temporal analysis of the active fleet.
40	
41	4. **Data Quality:** `ECCENTRICITY`, `BSTAR`, and `MEAN_MOTION_DOT` are stored as strings and require type conversion before numerical analysis. `MEAN_MOTION_DDOT` and `EPHEMERIS_TYPE` are nearly always 0 and carry little analytical value. No significant missing values are reported, but string-encoded scientific notation fields need careful parsing.
42	
43	5. **Starlink Dominance:** Approximately 6,000+ of the 14,875 satellites belong to SpaceX's Starlink constellation, which will heavily skew distributions unless filtered or segmented.

# Active Satellites Currently In Orbit (2026)

## About the Dataset

This dataset is a real-time catalog of **14,875 active satellites** currently orbiting Earth, sourced from the **CelesTrak** space-tracking platform via **NORAD** Two-Line Element (TLE) data. It was published on Kaggle (`ibrahimqasimi/active-satellites-currently-in-orbit`) and covers the full range of operational spacecraft — from mega-constellations like Starlink to individual science missions, weather satellites, GPS navigation satellites, reconnaissance platforms, and the International Space Station.

- **File:** `Active_Satellites_In_Orbit.csv`
- **Rows:** 14,875
- **Columns:** 17

## Column Schema

| Column Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| OBJECT_NAME | String | Satellite name (e.g., STARLINK-1234, ISS, GPS BIIR-2) |
| OBJECT_ID | String | International designator in format YYYY-NNNXXX (launch year, launch number, piece letter). Useful for extracting launch year. |
| EPOCH | String (datetime) | Date/time when the orbital element set was generated. Format: ISO 8601. Most entries are very recent. |
| MEAN_MOTION | Float | Number of orbits per day. Key for orbit classification: >14 ≈ LEO, ~1.0 ≈ GEO, between ≈ MEO. |
| ECCENTRICITY | String | Orbit shape factor (0 = perfectly circular, approaching 1 = highly elliptical). Stored as a string with leading decimal (e.g., ".002524"); needs conversion to float. |
| INCLINATION | Float | Orbital tilt relative to the equator in degrees (0° = equatorial, 90° = polar). |
| RA_OF_ASC_NODE | Float | Right ascension of the ascending node in degrees. |
| ARG_OF_PERICENTER | Float | Argument of perigee in degrees. |
| MEAN_ANOMALY | Float | Position of the satellite in its orbit at EPOCH, in degrees. |
| EPHEMERIS_TYPE | Integer | Always 0 in standard TLE data. |
| CLASSIFICATION_TYPE | String | Security classification ("U" = unclassified for most entries). |
| NORAD_CAT_ID | Integer | Unique NORAD catalog number for each object. |
| ELEMENT_SET_NO | Integer | Element set version number. |
| REV_AT_EPOCH | Integer | Revolution (orbit) count at the time of EPOCH. |
| BSTAR | String/Integer | Atmospheric drag coefficient (B* term). Stored in scientific notation as a string (e.g., ".64393E-3"); needs parsing. |
| MEAN_MOTION_DOT | String | First derivative of mean motion (drag term). Stored as a string. |
| MEAN_MOTION_DDOT | Integer | Second derivative of mean motion. Typically 0. |

## Key Analysis Notes

1. **Orbit Classification:** Use `MEAN_MOTION` to classify orbits. Satellites with >14 rev/day are in LEO (~160–2,000 km altitude). Those near 1.0 rev/day are in GEO (~35,786 km). Values between indicate MEO. Highly eccentric orbits (high `ECCENTRICITY`) with unusual mean motions may be HEO (e.g., Molniya orbits).

2. **Constellation Identification:** The `OBJECT_NAME` field contains constellation prefixes (e.g., "STARLINK-", "ONEWEB-", "IRIDIUM", "GPS"). Parsing these prefixes enables grouping by operator/constellation.

3. **Launch Year Extraction:** The first four characters of `OBJECT_ID` represent the launch year (e.g., "2024-" means launched in 2024). This enables temporal analysis of the active fleet.

4. **Data Quality:** `ECCENTRICITY`, `BSTAR`, and `MEAN_MOTION_DOT` are stored as strings and require type conversion before numerical analysis. `MEAN_MOTION_DDOT` and `EPHEMERIS_TYPE` are nearly always 0 and carry little analytical value. No significant missing values are reported, but string-encoded scientific notation fields need careful parsing.

5. **Starlink Dominance:** Approximately 6,000+ of the 14,875 satellites belong to SpaceX's Starlink constellation, which will heavily skew distributions unless filtered or segmented.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import csv
import re
from collections import defaultdict

# Load data
rows = []
with open('/app/benchmark/data.csv', 'r') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    for row in reader:
        rows.append(row)

print(f"Total rows: {len(rows)}")

# ─── KPIs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
total = len(rows)
print(f"\n=== KPIs ===")

# LEO: MEAN_MOTION > 14
leo = [r for r in rows if float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) > 14]
leo_share = round(len(leo)/total*100, 1)
print(f"Total Active Satellites: {total}")
print(f"LEO count (MM>14): {len(leo)} ({leo_share}%)")

# GEO: MEAN_MOTION ≈ 1.0 (0.9 to 1.1)
geo = [r for r in rows if 0.9 <= float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) <= 1.1]
print(f"GEO count (0.9<=MM<=1.1): {len(geo)} ({round(len(geo)/total*100,1)}%)")

# MEO: 1.1 < MM <= 14
meo = [r for r in rows if 1.1 < float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) <= 14]
print(f"MEO count: {len(meo)} ({round(len(meo)/total*100,1)}%)")

# HEO: MEAN_MOTION < 0.9 (or highly eccentric)
heo = [r for r in rows if float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) < 0.9]
heo_ecc = [r for r in rows if float(r['ECCENTRICITY'].lstrip('.')) > 0.4]
print(f"HEO count (MM<0.9): {len(heo)} ({round(len(heo)/total*100,1)}%)")

# Starlink
starlink = [r for r in rows if r['OBJECT_NAME'].upper().startswith('STARLINK')]
print(f"Starlink count: {len(starlink)}")

# Median inclination
inclinations = sorted([float(r['INCLINATION']) for r in rows])
n = len(inclinations)
median_inc = (inclinations[n//2] + inclinations[(n-1)//2]) / 2
print(f"Median Inclination: {median_inc:.2f}°")

# Launch year >= 2020
post2020 = []
for r in rows:
    oid = r['OBJECT_ID']
    year_match = re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', oid)
    if year_match:
        year = int(year_match.group(1))
        if year >= 2020:
            post2020.append(r)
print(f"Satellites launched since 2020: {len(post2020)}")

# ─── Orbital Regime Summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== Orbital Regime Classification ===")
print(f"LEO  (MM > 14.0):     {len(leo):5d}  ({len(leo)/total*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"MEO  (1.1 < MM <= 14): {len(meo):5d}  ({len(meo)/total*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"GEO  (0.9 <= MM <= 1.1): {len(geo):4d}  ({len(geo)/total*100:.1f}%)")
print(f"HEO  (MM < 0.9):     {len(heo):5d}  ({len(heo)/total*100:.1f}%)")

# ─── Constellation Breakdown ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== Major Constellation & Operator Breakdown ===")
operators = defaultdict(int)
for r in rows:
    name = r['OBJECT_NAME'].upper()
    if name.startswith('STARLINK'):
        operators['Starlink (SpaceX)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('ONEWEB') or name.startswith('ONE WEB'):
        operators['OneWeb'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('IRIDIUM'):
        operators['Iridium'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('GPS'):
        operators['GPS (USA)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('GLONASS'):
        operators['GLONASS (Russia)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('GALILEO'):
        operators['Galileo (EU)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('BEIDOU'):
        operators['BeiDou (China)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('O3B') or name.startswith('O3B MEO'):
        operators['O3b (SES)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('SES'):
        operators['SES'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('INTELSAT'):
        operators['Intelsat'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('EUTELSAT'):
        operators['Eutelsat'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('VIASAT'):
        operators['Viasat'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('Hughes'):
        operators['Hughes'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('CANopus') or name.startswith('CANOPUS'):
        operators['CANOPUS'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('Planet') or name.startswith('PLANET'):
        operators['Planet (Dove)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('SKYSAT'):
        operators['Planet (Skysat)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('RAPIDEYE') or name.startswith('RAPIDEYE'):
        operators['RapidEye'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('AQUA') or name.startswith('TERRA'):
        operators['NASA Earth Sci'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('NOAA'):
        operators['NOAA Weather'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('GOES'):
        operators['GOES Weather'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('METEOR'):
        operators['Russian Weather'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('COSMOS') or name.startswith('COSMOS'):
        operators['Cosmos (Russia)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('YAML') or name.startswith('YAM'):
        operators['Yam (Astra)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('ORBCOMM'):
        operators['Orbcomm'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('SWARM'):
        operators['Swarm (SpaceX)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('SPACEBEE') or name.startswith('SpaceBee'):
        operators['SpaceBee'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('FLOCK') or name.startswith('FLOCK'):
        operators['Planet (Flock)'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('LEO'):
        operators['SpaceX LEO'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('BLACKSKY') or name.startswith('BLACKSKY'):
        operators['BlackSky'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('TOMOPTER'):
        operators['TomoPlan'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('AST'):
        operators['AST SpaceMobile'] += 1
    elif name.startswith('OMN'):
        operators['OmniWeb'] += 1
    elif 'ISS' in name or name == 'ISS (ZARYA)':
        operators['ISS'] += 1
    elif 'TIANGONG' in name:
        operators['Tiangong (China)'] += 1
    else:
        operators['Other / Individual'] += 1

sorted_ops = sorted(operators.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])
for op, count in sorted_ops[:30]:
    pct = count/total*100
    bar = '█' * int(pct/2)
    print(f"  {op:<30} {count:5d} ({pct:5.1f}%) {bar}")

# ─── Launch Year Trends ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== Launch Year Trends ===")
launch_years = defaultdict(int)
for r in rows:
    oid = r['OBJECT_ID']
    year_match = re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', oid)
    if year_match:
        year = int(year_match.group(1))
        launch_years[year] += 1

sorted_years = sorted(launch_years.items())
for year, count in sorted_years:
    bar = '█' * int(count/100)
    print(f"  {year}: {count:5d}  {bar}")

# ─── Orbital Characteristics ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== Orbital Characteristics ===")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generates the satellite analysis HTML report.
"""
import csv, re, json
from collections import defaultdict

# ─── Load Data ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rows = []
with open('/app/benchmark/data.csv', 'r') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    for row in reader:
        rows.append(row)

total = len(rows)

# ─── KPIs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
leo = [r for r in rows if float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) > 14]
leo_count, leo_pct = len(leo), round(len(leo)/total*100, 1)

geo = [r for r in rows if 0.9 <= float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) <= 1.1]
geo_count, geo_pct = len(geo), round(len(geo)/total*100, 1)

meo = [r for r in rows if 1.1 < float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) <= 14]
meo_count, meo_pct = len(meo), round(len(meo)/total*100, 1)

heo = [r for r in rows if float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) < 0.9]
heo_count, heo_pct = len(heo), round(len(heo)/total*100, 1)

starlink = [r for r in rows if r['OBJECT_NAME'].upper().startswith('STARLINK')]
starlink_count = len(starlink)

inclinations = sorted([float(r['INCLINATION']) for r in rows])
n = len(inclinations)
median_inc = (inclinations[n//2] + inclinations[(n-1)//2]) / 2

post2020 = sum(1 for r in rows
               if re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', r['OBJECT_ID'])
               and int(re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', r['OBJECT_ID']).group(1)) >= 2020)

# ─── Launch Years ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
launch_years = defaultdict(int)
for r in rows:
    m = re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', r['OBJECT_ID'])
    if m:
        launch_years[int(m.group(1))] += 1

sorted_years = sorted(launch_years.items())

# ─── Operator Breakdown ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def classify_op(name):
    n = name.upper()
    if n.startswith('STARLINK'): return 'Starlink (SpaceX)'
    if n.startswith('ONEWEB') or n.startswith('ONE WEB'): return 'OneWeb'
    if n.startswith('IRIDIUM'): return 'Iridium'
    if n.startswith('GPS'): return 'GPS (USA)'
    if n.startswith('GLONASS'): return 'GLONASS (Russia)'
    if n.startswith('GALILEO'): return 'Galileo (EU)'
    if n.startswith('BEIDOU'): return 'BeiDou (China)'
    if n.startswith('O3B') or 'O3B MEO' in n: return 'O3b (SES)'

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Generates the satellite analysis HTML report.""" import csv, re, json as jsonmod from collections import defaultdict # ─── Load Data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── rows = [] with open('/app/benchmark/data.csv', 'r') as f: reader = csv.DictReader(f) for row in reader: rows.append(row) total = len(rows) # ─── KPIs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── leo = [r for r in rows if float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) > 14] leo_count, leo_pct = len(leo), round(len(leo)/total*100, 1) geo = [r for r in rows if 0.9 <= float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) <= 1.1] geo_count, geo_pct = len(geo), round(len(geo)/total*100, 1) meo = [r for r in rows if 1.1 < float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) <= 14] meo_count, meo_pct = len(meo), round(len(meo)/total*100, 1) heo = [r for r in rows if float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) < 0.9] heo_count, heo_pct = len(heo), round(len(heo)/total*100, 1) starlink = [r for r in rows if r['OBJECT_NAME'].upper().startswith('STARLINK')] starlink_count = len(starlink) inclinations = sorted([float(r['INCLINATION']) for r in rows]) n = len(inclinations) median_inc = (inclinations[n//2] + inclinations[(n-1)//2]) / 2 post2020 = sum( 1 for r in rows if re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', r['OBJECT_ID']) and int(re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', r['OBJECT_ID']).group(1)) >= 2020 ) # ─── Launch Years ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── launch_years = defaultdict(int) for r in rows: m = re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', r['OBJECT_ID']) if m: launch_years[int(m.group(1))] += 1 sorted_years = sorted(launch_years.items()) launch_year_labels = [str(y) for y, _ in sorted_years] launch_year_values = [v for _, v in sorted_years] # Cumulative cum_vals = [] running = 0 for _, v in sorted_years: running += v cum_vals.append(running) launch_year_ints = [y for y, _ in sorted_years] # ─── Operator Breakdown ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── def classify_op(name): n = name.upper() if n.startswith('STARLINK'): return 'Starlink (SpaceX)' if n.startswith('ONEWEB') or n.startswith('ONE WEB'): return 'OneWeb' if n.startswith('IRIDIUM'): return 'Iridium' if n.startswith('GPS'): return 'GPS (USA)' if n.startswith('GLONASS'): return 'GLONASS (Russia)' if n.startswith('GALILEO'): return 'Galileo (EU)' if n.startswith('BEIDOU'): return 'BeiDou (China)' if n.startswith('O3B') or 'O3B MEO' in n: return 'O3b (SES)' if n.startswith('SES '): return 'SES' if n.startswith('INTELSAT'): return 'Intelsat' if n.startswith('EUTELSAT'): return 'Eutelsat' if n.startswith('VIASAT'): return 'Viasat' if n.startswith('HUGHES'): return 'Hughes' if n.startswith('CANOPUS'): return 'CANOPUS' if n.startswith('PLANET') or n.startswith('FLOCK'): return 'Planet (Flock/Skysat)' if n.startswith('SKYSAT'): return 'Planet (Skysat)' if n.startswith('RAPIDEYE'): return 'RapidEye' if n.startswith('AQUA') or n.startswith('TERRA'): return 'NASA Earth Science' if n.startswith('NOAA'): return 'NOAA Weather' if n.startswith('GOES'): return 'GOES Weather' if n.startswith('METEOR'): return 'Russian Weather' if n.startswith('COSMOS'): return 'Cosmos (Russia)' if n.startswith('YAML') or n.startswith('YAM'): return 'Yam (Astra)' if n.startswith('ORBCOMM'): return 'Orbcomm' if n.startswith('SWARM'): return 'Swarm (SpaceX)' if n.startswith('SPACEBEE'): return 'SpaceBee' if n.startswith('BLACKSKY') or n.startswith('BLACKSKY'): return 'BlackSky' if n.startswith('AST'): return 'AST SpaceMobile' if n.startswith('OMNI') or n.startswith('OMN'): return 'OmniWeb' if 'ISS' in n or n == 'ISS (ZARYA)': return 'ISS' if 'TIANGONG' in n: return 'Tiangong (China)' if n.startswith('LEO ') or n.startswith('LEO-') or n.startswith('GSE'): return 'SpaceX LEO' if n.startswith('LEMUR') or n.startswith('LEMUR'): return 'Lemur (Spaceflight)' if n.startswith('SHERPA') or n.startswith('SHERPA'): return 'Sherpa' if n.startswith('TRUCK') or n.startswith('TRUCK'): return 'Space Truck' return 'Other / Individual' operators = defaultdict(int) for r in rows: operators[classify_op(r['OBJECT_NAME'])] += 1 sorted_ops = sorted(operators.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]) top_ops = sorted_ops[:15] # ─── Inclination Breakdown ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── inc_buckets = defaultdict(int) for r in rows: inc = float(r['INCLINATION']) bucket = int(inc // 10) * 10 inc_buckets[bucket] += 1 inc_labels = sorted(inc_buckets.keys()) inc_values = [inc_buckets[k] for k in inc_labels] # ─── Mean Motion Histogram ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── mm_hist = defaultdict(int) for r in rows: mm = float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) bucket = round(mm, 1) mm_hist[bucket] += 1 mm_sorted = sorted(mm_hist.items()) mm_hist_labels = [str(k) for k, _ in mm_sorted] mm_hist_values = [v for _, v in mm_sorted] # ─── Eccentricity buckets ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── ecc_buckets = {'< 0.01': 0, '0.01\u20130.05': 0, '0.05\u20130.10': 0, '0.10\u20130.30': 0, '0.30\u20130.60': 0, '\u2265 0.60': 0} for r in rows: try: ecc = float('.' + r['ECCENTRICITY'].lstrip('.')) if ecc < 0.01: ecc_buckets['< 0.01'] += 1 elif ecc < 0.05: ecc_buckets['0.01\u20130.05'] += 1 elif ecc < 0.10: ecc_buckets['0.05\u20130.10'] += 1 elif ecc < 0.30: ecc_buckets['0.10\u20130.30'] += 1 elif ecc < 0.60: ecc_buckets['0.30\u20130.60'] += 1 else: ecc_buckets['\u2265 0.60'] += 1 except: pass ecc_labels = list(ecc_buckets.keys()) ecc_values = list(ecc_buckets.values()) # ─── Starlink Inclination ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── starlink_inc_buckets = defaultdict(int) for r in starlink: inc = float(r['INCLINATION']) bucket = int(inc // 5) * 5 starlink_inc_buckets[bucket] += 1 s_inc_labels = sorted(starlink_inc_buckets.keys()) s_inc_values = [starlink_inc_buckets[k] for k in #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Generates the satellite analysis HTML report.""" import csv, re, json as jsonmod from collections import defaultdict # ─── Load Data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── rows = [] with open('/app/benchmark/data.csv', 'r') as f: reader = csv.DictReader(f) for row in reader: rows.append(row) total = len(rows) # ─── KPIs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── leo = [r for r in rows if float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) > 14] leo_count, leo_pct = len(leo), round(len(leo)/total*100, 1) geo = [r for r in rows if 0.9 <= float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) <= 1.1] geo_count, geo_pct = len(geo), round(len(geo)/total*100, 1) meo = [r for r in rows if 1.1 < float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) <= 14] meo_count, meo_pct = len(meo), round(len(meo)/total*100, 1) heo = [r for r in rows if float(r['MEAN_MOTION']) < 0.9] heo_count, heo_pct = len(heo), round(len(heo)/total*100, 1) starlink = [r for r in rows if r['OBJECT_NAME'].upper().startswith('STARLINK')] starlink_count = len(starlink) inclinations = sorted([float(r['INCLINATION']) for r in rows]) n = len(inclinations) median_inc = (inclinations[n//2] + inclinations[(n-1)//2]) / 2 post2020 = sum( 1 for r in rows if re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', r['OBJECT_ID']) and int(re.match(r'^(\d{4})-', 01

Catalog Overview & Key Figures

The CelesTrak/NORAD TLE catalog captures 14,875 active satellites as of March–April 2026. Epoch dates concentrated in March 2026 confirm data freshness. The catalog excludes debris and non-operational objects. Mean motion ranges from 0.28 rev/day (HEO) to 16.30 rev/day (lowest LEO), with 86.5% of all objects in LEO (mean motion > 14.0) and a median inclination of 53.2°.

LEO Dominance. The 86.5% LEO share reflects the extraordinary scale of mega-constellation deployment — primarily Starlink, OneWeb, and Planet — concentrated in shells between ~550 km and ~1,200 km altitude. GEO (4.0%) remains a premium, high-value orbit for communications, weather, and intelligence satellites.
03

Major Constellation & Operator Breakdown

SpaceX's Starlink constellation dominates the active satellite population, accounting for 67.8% of all active satellites. The remaining ~32% is split across commercial, civil, and government operators. This extreme concentration fundamentally skews orbital statistics toward LEO and low-inclination shells.

Top 15 Operators by Satellite Count
Starlink Shell Inclination Breakdown (n=10,083)
Non-Starlink Operators — Share of Remaining 4,792 Satellites
Starlink Shell Strategy. SpaceX operates multiple orbital shells differentiated by inclination: the 53.2° shell (~4,840 sats) covers mid-latitude global coverage; the 40° shell (~3,656 sats) adds polar coverage; and the 97.6° shell (~872 sats) provides high-latitude reinforcement. Shells at 70° (~506 sats) and 65° (~209 sats) address regional coverage gaps. This multi-shell approach makes Starlink's inclination distribution multimodal, producing the overall LEO median inclination of ~53°.
04

Launch Year Trends — The Great Acceleration

Of the 14,875 active satellites, 13,461 (90.5%) were launched since 2020. The 2025 active fleet alone accounts for 4,329 satellites — more than the combined total of all spacecraft launched before 2018. The growth from 498 (2020) to 4,329 (2025) represents an 8.7× increase in five years.

Policy Implication. The launch cadence has shifted from ~50–100 new active satellites/year throughout the 2000s–2010s to thousands per year, driven almost entirely by commercial LEO constellations. Regulatory frameworks, spectrum allocation, and orbital debris mitigation rules written before 2018 face a fundamentally different operational environment. If 2025's pace continues, the active LEO population could exceed 20,000 by 2030.
05

Inclination Modal Structure. The inclination distribution is distinctly bimodal: the peak at 50°–60° (5,399 sats, 36.3%) reflects Starlink's dominant 53.2° shell; a secondary peak at 40°–50° (3,915 sats, 26.3%) blends Starlink's 40° shell with OneWeb's ~86° polar constellation. The ~0°–10° band (584 sats) is dominated by GEO-belt and equatorial-orbit satellites. High-inclination HEO satellites (Molniya-class) appear in the 60°–70° band.
06

Key Takeaways & Outlook

  • 1
    Mega-constellations have fundamentally restructured Earth orbit. A single operator — SpaceX Starlink — accounts for 67.8% of all active satellites. The top five operators (Starlink, OneWeb, Planet, Cosmos, Iridium) represent ~74% of the active population. Spectrum allocation and orbital congestion policy cannot be discussed without Starlink as the central case.
  • 2
    LEO is the operational frontier. With 86.5% of active satellites in LEO, medium and high Earth orbit regimes remain relatively uncongested. The crowding challenge is almost exclusively a LEO problem — concentrated in two inclination bands (40°–60°) at altitudes between ~550 km and ~1,200 km.
  • 3
    The launch growth curve is near-vertical since 2020. From 498 active satellites launched in 2020 to 4,329 in 2025 — an 8.7× increase in five years. This rate of change outpaces the revision cycles of ITU spectrum regulations and national licensing frameworks.
  • 4
    Debris risk is increasingly a Starlink-specific concern. With 10,083 active Starlink satellites, SpaceX's own conjunction management practices effectively define the debris environment in heavily used shells. The FCC's 2022 five-year post-mission disposal rule for LEO satellites below 2,000 km is a significant step, but enforcement and international harmonization remain open questions.
  • 5
    Inclination stratification creates distinct congestion zones. Starlink's multi-shell strategy (40°, 53°, 65°, 70°, 97° shells) deliberately fills different latitudinal coverage bands — but specific inclination corridors face disproportionate conjunction density. Operators planning new constellations face a de facto zoning problem: certain shells are becoming crowded while others remain available.
